exchange.sent: What evidence is required to compare our Signaling / Non-signaling Tester solution with a competitor for AI without making unsupported claims?

answer.answer:
已查到可引用的部分資料：

### Short answer
To compare an R&S Signaling / Non-signaling Tester solution with a competitor for AI without unsupported claims, the evidence needs to include formal R&S product/configuration evidence, formal competitor product/configuration evidence, AI test methodology and results, and a same-scope comparison basis; current sources mostly identify gaps, sales-positioning limits, or PR/demo-level evidence rather than a verified AI competitor comparison [26][30][63][70].
### Evidence required
| Evidence needed | Why it is required |
|---|---|
| Formal R&S specifications and features documents for the exact tester configuration, because CMX500 formal specifications come from `CMX500_specs_en_5216-4127-22_v1100` Version 11.00, while `CMX500_Features_CSW9-20-0_en_32` is a features/functions overview and “data without tolerance limits is not binding” [70]. | This prevents treating non-binding feature wording or sales wording as a technical specification [70]. |
| Exact R&S signaling options, order numbers, dependencies, and scope, because the CMX500 features source lists specific LTE / NR / WLAN signaling options such as R&S CMX-KS500B/M/X, CMX-KS600B/M/X, CMX-KS617B/M/X, CMX-KS627B/M/X, and WLAN options CMX-KS350B through CMX-KS365B [72][73]. | This prevents a generic “signaling tester supports it” claim when the support depends on specific options and feature scope [72][73]. |
| Formal evidence for any non-signaling production path, because the 5G device testing value chain includes “Non-signaling RF,” but the battle-card production-path claims for CMP180 / CMP200 / CMW100 are sales-positioning and the formal platform specifications must be cited separately [40][23][24]. | This prevents using a competitor battle card as proof of non-signaling production capability or scalability [23][24]. |
| AI-specific test methodology, test case definitions, model / terminal / server environment, network scenario profiles, statistical confidence, and result tables, because the generative AI user experience testing source explicitly says those items are not provided [26]. | This is needed before comparing AI performance or AI user experience across solutions [26]. |
| A standardized or accepted benchmark / framework, because the generative AI user experience testing source says the industry still lacks mature metrics and standardized test frameworks for evaluating generative AI application user experience [25]. | This prevents presenting a demo metric as an industry-standard AI benchmark [25]. |
| Clear separation between PR/demo evidence and product specification evidence, because the generative AI testbed source is PR / demonstration-level evidence and not a formal test specification, standardized benchmark, or product datasheet [26]. | This prevents using the CMX500 generative-AI demo as if it were a binding product spec or benchmark [26]. |
| If the AI context is AI server / data-center hardware rather than generative-AI UE testing, formal setup, options, fixtures, frequency, calibration, and application-note evidence are required, because the AI server R&S solution mapping is only sales / test-solution mapping and not a formal product configuration or verified opportunity [1][63][64]. | This prevents using an Excel mapping as proof of product fit, customer adoption, purchase, or validated test configuration [1][63]. |
| Competitor official datasheets, feature documents, option lists, versions, release status, and test conditions, because the Keysight battle-card page says Keysight UXM descriptions need Keysight official or third-party verification and lack formal datasheets, option codes, release status, and test conditions [13]. | This prevents making competitor capability claims from R&S internal positioning alone [13][30]. |
| Third-party or competitor-official evidence for any competitor weakness or advantage, because the R&S vs Keysight, R&S vs Anritsu, and R&S vs amarisoft pages state that internal battle-card claims are sales positioning, not binding technical specifications [28][19][22]. | This prevents treating “only platform,” “leadership,” “lower TCO,” or “fewer boxes” language as verifiable technical specifications [30][21][24]. |
| For Anritsu Virtual Signalling Tester comparisons, Anritsu official product evidence can describe MX844030PC as a PC-based software protocol simulator for NR / RedCap protocol testing, with MAC-IF, PHY-IF Digital-IQ, and RF-IF configurations, but its limitations include missing full test-case lists, release coverage, conformance status, and throughput metrics [11][75][78]. | This prevents over-extending Anritsu brochure facts into unsupported performance, conformance, or throughput comparisons [78]. |
| For Keysight AI-related claims, official evidence is needed for Atlas, RaySim, Channel Studio, and UXM capabilities, because current Keysight AI / UXM tool descriptions come from an R&S battle card and lack official versions or functional boundaries [83][30]. | This prevents claiming a verified AI-toolchain advantage or disadvantage without Keysight-source or third-party evidence [83][30]. |
| For RFU18 / FR3 / 6G-related AI or future-readiness comparisons, formal RFU18 datasheet, order number, supported configurations, bandwidth, software release, and measurement conditions are required, because current RFU18 / FR3 sources include PR or comparison-table claims and explicitly lack complete formal specifications and test conditions [37][39][51][53]. | This prevents converting PR/demo claims such as “up to 18 GHz” into unrestricted CMX500 base-system specifications [51][53]. |
### Minimum comparison package
| Area | Required evidence package |
|---|---|
| R&S signaling solution | CMX500 formal specifications, CMX500 features/options list, exact software version, licenses, hardware configuration, order numbers, and test conditions [70][72][73]. |
| R&S non-signaling solution | Formal specifications for the non-signaling platform and production setup, because current passages only identify non-signaling as a value-chain test type and battle-card production-path claims require separate formal platform evidence [40][23][24]. |
| AI test claim | AI benchmark or methodology with test cases, LLM / application model, DUT / terminal, server or cloud setup, network scenario profiles, statistical confidence, and result tables [25][26]. |
| Competitor claim | Competitor official datasheets / feature documents / option codes / versions / release status / test conditions, or third-party verification, because internal R&S battle cards are not binding competitor specifications [13][30][21][24]. |
| Head-to-head comparison | Same test scope, same configurations, same conditions, and traceable results are needed, because the current cited sources either provide R&S product facts, competitor sales positioning, PR demonstrations, or mapping leads, but not a verified AI head-to-head comparison [26][28][30][63]. |
### Unsupported without that evidence
Claims that R&S is “better,” “only,” “more integrated,” “lower TCO,” “fewer boxes,” or has competitor leadership cannot be used as verified technical claims when they come from sales battle cards, because the cited pages explicitly classify those phrases as sales language or internal positioning rather than binding specifications [30][21][24][87].

### Short answer
To compare an R&S Signaling / Non-signaling Tester solution with a competitor for AI without unsupported claims, the evidence needs to include formal R&S product/configuration evidence, formal competitor product/configuration evidence, AI test methodology and results, and a same-scope comparison basis; current sources mostly identify gaps, sales-positioning limits, or PR/demo-level evidence rather than a verified AI competitor comparison [26][30][63][70].
### Evidence required
| Evidence needed | Why it is required |
|---|---|
| Formal R&S specifications and features documents for the exact tester configuration, because CMX500 formal specifications come from `CMX500_specs_en_5216-4127-22_v1100` Version 11.00, while `CMX500_Features_CSW9-20-0_en_32` is a features/functions overview and “data without tolerance limits is not binding” [70]. | This prevents treating non-binding feature wording or sales wording as a technical specification [70]. |
| Exact R&S signaling options, order numbers, dependencies, and scope, because the CMX500 features source lists specific LTE / NR / WLAN signaling options such as R&S CMX-KS500B/M/X, CMX-KS600B/M/X, CMX-KS617B/M/X, CMX-KS627B/M/X, and WLAN options CMX-KS350B through CMX-KS365B [72][73]. | This prevents a generic “signaling tester supports it” claim when the support depends on specific options and feature scope [72][73]. |
| Formal evidence for any non-signaling production path, because the 5G device testing value chain includes “Non-signaling RF,” but the battle-card production-path claims for CMP180 / CMP200 / CMW100 are sales-positioning and the formal platform specifications must be cited separately [40][23][24]. | This prevents using a competitor battle card as proof of non-signaling production capability or scalability [23][24]. |
| AI-specific test methodology, test case definitions, model / terminal / server environment, network scenario profiles, statistical confidence, and result tables, because the generative AI user experience testing source explicitly says those items are not provided [26]. | This is needed before comparing AI performance or AI user experience across solutions [26]. |
| A standardized or accepted benchmark / framework, because the generative AI user experience testing source says the industry still lacks mature metrics and standardized test frameworks for evaluating generative AI application user experience [25]. | This prevents presenting a demo metric as an industry-standard AI benchmark [25]. |
| Clear separation between PR/demo evidence and product specification evidence, because the generative AI testbed source is PR / demonstration-level evidence and not a formal test specification, standardized benchmark, or product datasheet [26]. | This prevents using the CMX500 generative-AI demo as if it were a binding product spec or benchmark [26]. |
| If the AI context is AI server / data-center hardware rather than generative-AI UE testing, formal setup, options, fixtures, frequency, calibration, and application-note evidence are required, because the AI server R&S solution mapping is only sales / test-solution mapping and not a formal product configuration or verified opportunity [1][63][64]. | This prevents using an Excel mapping as proof of product fit, customer adoption, purchase, or validated test configuration [1][63]. |
| Competitor official datasheets, feature documents, option lists, versions, release status, and test conditions, because the Keysight battle-card page says Keysight UXM descriptions need Keysight official or third-party verification and lack formal datasheets, option codes, release status, and test conditions [13]. | This prevents making competitor capability claims from R&S internal positioning alone [13][30]. |
| Third-party or competitor-official evidence for any competitor weakness or advantage, because the R&S vs Keysight, R&S vs Anritsu, and R&S vs amarisoft pages state that internal battle-card claims are sales positioning, not binding technical specifications [28][19][22]. | This prevents treating “only platform,” “leadership,” “lower TCO,” or “fewer boxes” language as verifiable technical specifications [30][21][24]. |
| For Anritsu Virtual Signalling Tester comparisons, Anritsu official product evidence can describe MX844030PC as a PC-based software protocol simulator for NR / RedCap protocol testing, with MAC-IF, PHY-IF Digital-IQ, and RF-IF configurations, but its limitations include missing full test-case lists, release coverage, conformance status, and throughput metrics [11][75][78]. | This prevents over-extending Anritsu brochure facts into unsupported performance, conformance, or throughput comparisons [78]. |
| For Keysight AI-related claims, official evidence is needed for Atlas, RaySim, Channel Studio, and UXM capabilities, because current Keysight AI / UXM tool descriptions come from an R&S battle card and lack official versions or functional boundaries [83][30]. | This prevents claiming a verified AI-toolchain advantage or disadvantage without Keysight-source or third-party evidence [83][30]. |
| For RFU18 / FR3 / 6G-related AI or future-readiness comparisons, formal RFU18 datasheet, order number, supported configurations, bandwidth, software release, and measurement conditions are required, because current RFU18 / FR3 sources include PR or comparison-table claims and explicitly lack complete formal specifications and test conditions [37][39][51][53]. | This prevents converting PR/demo claims such as “up to 18 GHz” into unrestricted CMX500 base-system specifications [51][53]. |
### Minimum comparison package
| Area | Required evidence package |
|---|---|
| R&S signaling solution | CMX500 formal specifications, CMX500 features/options list, exact software version, licenses, hardware configuration, order numbers, and test conditions [70][72][73]. |
| R&S non-signaling solution | Formal specifications for the non-signaling platform and production setup, because current passages only identify non-signaling as a value-chain test type and battle-card production-path claims require separate formal platform evidence [40][23][24]. |

Claims that R&S is “better,” “only,” “more integrated,” “lower TCO,” “fewer boxes,” or has competitor leadership cannot be used as verified technical claims when they come from sales battle cards, because the cited pages explicitly classify those phrases as sales language or internal positioning rather than binding specifications [30][21][24][87].

依 [[CMX500_specs_en_5216-4127-22_v1100]]，[[R&S CMX500]] 是 universal one-box network emulation and measurement test solution，支援最新 3GPP [[5G NR]] technology，適用於 device testing，涵蓋 [[LTE]]、[[NR FR1]]、[[NR FR2]]，並支援 non-standalone（NSA）、standalone（SA）、FDD 與 TDD。

依 [[CMX500_Features_CSW9-20-0_en_32]]，[[R&S CMX500]] 也提供：

- [[NR FR1]] / [[NR FR2]] signaling 與 TX measurements。
- [[LTE]] signaling、LTE-DTC / direct-to-cell communication、LTE measurements。
- [[NB-IoT]] / NB-NTN signaling。
- [[WLAN]] signaling 與 WLAN TX measurements，涵蓋 802.11a/b/g/n/ac、802.11ax、802.11be、802.11bn 與 2x2 MIMO。
- [[Fading]]、[[AWGN]]、[[BLER]]、[[CSI report]]、[[Throughput measurement]]、[[PER measurement]]。
- Application test、IP traffic analysis、IMS / audio / [[POLQA]]。
- GUI、graphical scripting、Python-based [[XLAPI]] 與 [[SCPI]] remote control。

R&S CMX500

- R&S CMX-KA100 提供 internal IP services 與 IP connection to DUT 測試 applications，包含 DNS、IMS、Message Center、FTP、HTTP、DNS monitor、IP logging、iPerf、Ping、throughput、Max Throughput Wizard、web server。
- R&S CMX-KA110 增強 KA100，加入 QoS、ePDG、N3IWF、delay measurement、IP tune tool、SMPP / MT SMS advanced settings。
- R&S CMX-KA150 提供 IP analysis tool，用於監控與分析 DUT uplink / downlink IP traffic。
- R&S CMX-KA180 提供 audio codecs for 4G and 5G IMS voice call，支援 AMR-NB、AMR-WB、EVS，並包含 [[R&S CMX-ZG180A]] external sound card drivers and configuration settings。
- R&S CMX-KA181 加入 [[POLQA]]，用於 measuring perceived speech quality；measurement version 為 3，mode 為 full-band 或 narrowband。
- R&S CMX-KA401 支援 WAV player / recorder、upload/download WAV files、file-based POLQA measurements 與 end-to-end audio delay。

[[Virtual Signalling Tester]] 則是 [[mx844030pc-j1200]] 中 Anritsu NR / RedCap protocol simulation and test product / solution 語彙。兩者名稱相近，但目前沒有來源支持它們是同一產品、同一架構或同一市場分類。

Virtual Signalling Tester › 來源定義

- [[RRC-NAS]]
- [[PDCP]]
- [[RLC]]
- [[MAC]]

來源主張它可不使用一般硬體測試儀而在 PC 上快速建立 protocol test environment；但 RF-IF configuration 仍使用 [[Anritsu MD8190A]] Universal RF Unit 與 [[MX819020A]] RF Platform。

- 支援快速 functional test、regression test、sample scenario parameterization、test procedure 與 report / log display。
- 來源列出 [[5G RedCap]]、Automotive、Healthcare、Industrial IoT、Smart Cities 等應用語境。

- 來源列出的 Anritsu 產品組合包含 [[Anritsu MT8000A]]（5G NR FR1/FR2/FR3）、[[Anritsu MD8475B]]（LTE/IMS/eCall）、[[Anritsu MT8821C]]（LTE/LTE-A/3G/2G RF）、[[Anritsu MT8862A]]（Wi-Fi）與 [[Anritsu MT8852B]]（Bluetooth）。
- 來源稱 [[Anritsu MT8000A]] 需要 separate RF boards for FR1/FR2/FR3、external mmWave converters，並列出 boards 021/022/023/024/031/032/033；後文 weakness 另列 041，兩處 board list 不完全一致。
- 來源稱 Anritsu new FR3 option / module 覆蓋 **0.4–16 GHz**，並認為它相較 R&S upcoming [[RFU18]] / 18 GHz headroom 有 future-proofing 限制。
- R&S positioning statement：[[R&S CMX500]] 被定位為 single integrated platform，涵蓋 FR1 + FR2 + FR3、fading、IP throughput、NTN、Wi-Fi、RF analysis 與 signaling；Anritsu 被描述為需要 RF boards、external mmWave converters、multiple boxes 與 fragmented software tools。
- 來源列出的 R&S differentiators 包含 one-platform architecture、integrated fading + IP throughput、unified software ecosystem、FR2 / FR3 performance leadership、cellular + Wi-Fi single platform，以及 R&D → conformance → production path。
- 來源的 sales landmines 聚焦在 FR1 wideband beyond 400 MHz、FR1+FR2+FR3+WLAN+LTE one-box、integrated fading + IP load、unified software、multi-cell / CA / mobility without extra boxes，以及 FR3 frequency headroom beyond 16 GHz。
- 來源的 R&S offensive plays 包含 one-box FR1 + FR2 + FR3 + WLAN + fading + IP、FR2 / FR3 performance leadership、integrated WLAN signaling、R&D → conformance → production lifecycle、future-proof RedCap / NTN / ORAN / 6G、unified software ecosystem，以及 fewer boxes / lower TCO / higher throughput 的簡化訊息。

[[FR3 測試與 RFU18 battle card 主張]] 指 R&S sales battle cards 中以 [[R&S CMX500]] / upcoming [[RFU18]] 對比競品 FR3 / 6G path 的銷售定位說法；它不是正式 RFU18 或 CMX500 specifications。[[Rohde & Schwarz and Qualcomm unlock potential of proposed FR3 frequency range for next generation 6G wireless networks]] 另提供一個 PR / demonstration-level 來源，說 [[R&S CMX500 OBT]] 在 13 GHz 驗證 [[5G NR]] high-throughput performance，但該 PR 同樣不是 formal CMX500 / RFU18 specifications。[[Rohde & Schwarz demonstrates FR1–FR3 carrier aggregation, advancing 6G readiness]] 進一步提供 PR 層級來源，明確把 new [[RFU18]] board、CMX500 coverage up to 18 GHz 與 FR1-FR3 carrier aggregation demo 連在一起；但它仍未提供 RFU18 formal datasheet、order number 或完整 test conditions。

- [[R&S CMX500]] 3GPP RF pre-conformance WebGUI solution 提供執行 **NR-FR1 Standalone（SA）** test cases 的平台，依據 [[3GPP TS 38.521-1]] specification。

- Test case procedures 針對 R&D use cases 最佳化，使用 specification 中最相關的 configurations。

- Pre-conformance testing 目標是在基於 [[3GPP]] specification 的 streamlined procedure 中提供 meaningful results，但不嚴格遵循所有 parameters。
- 嚴格的 RF conformance testing 與 validated test cases 可使用 [[R&S TS8980 Conformance Test Platform]]。

### Short answer
To compare an R&S Signaling / Non-signaling Tester solution with a competitor for AI without unsupported claims, the evidence needs to include formal R&S product/configuration evidence, formal competitor product/configuration evidence, AI test methodology and results, and a same-scope comparison basis; current sources mostly identify gaps, sales-positioning limits, or PR/demo-level evidence rather than a verified AI competitor comparison [26][30][63][70].
### Evidence required
| Evidence needed | Why it is required |
|---|---|
| Formal R&S specifications and features documents for the exact tester configuration, because CMX500 formal specifications come from `CMX500_specs_en_5216-4127-22_v1100` Version 11.00, while `CMX500_Features_CSW9-20-0_en_32` is a features/functions overview and “data without tolerance limits is not binding” [70]. | This prevents treating non-binding feature wording or sales wording as a technical specification [70]. |
| Exact R&S signaling options, order numbers, dependencies, and scope, because the CMX500 features source lists specific LTE / NR / WLAN signaling options such as R&S CMX-KS500B/M/X, CMX-KS600B/M/X, CMX-KS617B/M/X, CMX-KS627B/M/X, and WLAN options CMX-KS350B through CMX-KS365B [72][73]. | This prevents a generic “signaling tester supports it” claim when the support depends on specific options and feature scope [72][73]. |
| Formal evidence for any non-signaling production path, because the 5G device testing value chain includes “Non-signaling RF,” but the battle-card production-path claims for CMP180 / CMP200 / CMW100 are sales-positioning and the formal platform specifications must be cited separately [40][23][24]. | This prevents using a competitor battle card as proof of non-signaling production capability or scalability [23][24]. |
| AI-specific test methodology, test case definitions, model / terminal / server environment, network scenario profiles, statistical confidence, and result tables, because the generative AI user experience testing source explicitly says those items are not provided [26]. | This is needed before comparing AI performance or AI user experience across solutions [26]. |
| A standardized or accepted benchmark / framework, because the generative AI user experience testing source says the industry still lacks mature metrics and standardized test frameworks for evaluating generative AI application user experience [25]. | This prevents presenting a demo metric as an industry-standard AI benchmark [25]. |
| Clear separation between PR/demo evidence and product specification evidence, because the generative AI testbed source is PR / demonstration-level evidence and not a formal test specification, standardized benchmark, or product datasheet [26]. | This prevents using the CMX500 generative-AI demo as if it were a binding product spec or benchmark [26]. |
| If the AI context is AI server / data-center hardware rather than generative-AI UE testing, formal setup, options, fixtures, frequency, calibration, and application-note evidence are required, because the AI server R&S solution mapping is only sales / test-solution mapping and not a formal product configuration or verified opportunity [1][63][64]. | This prevents using an Excel mapping as proof of product fit, customer adoption, purchase, or validated test configuration [1][63]. |
| Competitor official datasheets, feature documents, option lists, versions, release status, and test conditions, because the Keysight battle-card page says Keysight UXM descriptions need Keysight official or third-party verification and lack formal datasheets, option codes, release status, and test conditions [13]. | This prevents making competitor capability claims from R&S internal positioning alone [13][30]. |
| Third-party or competitor-official evidence for any competitor weakness or advantage, because the R&S vs Keysight, R&S vs Anritsu, and R&S vs amarisoft pages state that internal battle-card claims are sales positioning, not binding technical specifications [28][19][22]. | This prevents treating “only platform,” “leadership,” “lower TCO,” or “fewer boxes” language as verifiable technical specifications [30][21][24]. |
| For Anritsu Virtual Signalling Tester comparisons, Anritsu official product evidence can describe MX844030PC as a PC-based software protocol simulator for NR / RedCap protocol testing, with MAC-IF, PHY-IF Digital-IQ, and RF-IF configurations, but its limitations include missing full test-case lists, release coverage, conformance status, and throughput metrics [11][75][78]. | This prevents over-extending Anritsu brochure facts into unsupported performance, conformance, or throughput comparisons [78]. |
| For Keysight AI-related claims, official evidence is needed for Atlas, RaySim, Channel Studio, and UXM capabilities, because current Keysight AI / UXM tool descriptions come from an R&S battle card and lack official versions or functional boundaries [83][30]. | This prevents claiming a verified AI-toolchain advantage or disadvantage without Keysight-source or third-party evidence [83][30]. |
| For RFU18 / FR3 / 6G-related AI or future-readiness comparisons, formal RFU18 datasheet, order number, supported configurations, bandwidth, software release, and measurement conditions are required, because current RFU18 / FR3 sources include PR or comparison-table claims and explicitly lack complete formal specifications and test conditions [37][39][51][53]. | This prevents converting PR/demo claims such as “up to 18 GHz” into unrestricted CMX500 base-system specifications [51][53]. |
### Minimum comparison package
| Area | Required evidence package |
|---|---|
| R&S signaling solution | CMX500 formal specifications, CMX500 features/options list, exact software version, licenses, hardware configuration, order numbers, and test conditions [70][72][73]. |
| R&S non-signaling solution | Formal specifications for the non-signaling platform and production setup, because current passages only identify non-signaling as a value-chain test type and battle-card production-path claims require separate formal platform evidence [40][23][24]. |
| AI test claim | AI benchmark or methodology with test cases, LLM / application model, DUT / terminal, server or cloud setup, network scenario profiles, statistical confidence, and result tables [25][26]. |
| Competitor claim | Competitor official datasheets / feature documents / option codes / versions / release status / test conditions, or third-party verification, because internal R&S battle cards are not binding competitor specifications [13][30][21][24]. |
| Head-to-head comparison | Same test scope, same configurations, same conditions, and traceable results are needed, because the current cited sources either provide R&S product facts, competitor sales positioning, PR demonstrations, or mapping leads, but not a verified AI head-to-head comparison [26][28][30][63]. |
### Unsupported without that evidence
Claims that R&S is “better,” “only,” “more integrated,” “lower TCO,” “fewer boxes,” or has competitor leadership cannot be used as verified technical claims when they come from sales battle cards, because the cited pages explicitly classify those phrases as sales language or internal positioning rather than binding specifications [30][21][24][87].
